items.informal_name: Injectivity of Taylor Series Expansion at $ r $
items.type: ∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Ring R] (r : R), Function.Injective ⇑(Polynomial.taylor r)
items.informal_description: The Taylor series expansion map at $ r $, which sends a polynomial $ f(X) $ to $ f(X + r) $, is injective as a linear transformation on the polynomial ring $ R[X] $.

items.informal_name: Injectivity of the Taylor Series Expansion at r
items.type: ∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Ring R] {r : R} {p q : Polynomial R}, (Polynomial.taylor r) p = (Polynomial.taylor r) q ↔ p = q
items.informal_description: For any element $ r $ in a semiring $ R $ and polynomials $ p, q \in R[X] $, the equality $ \text{Taylor}_r(p) = \text{Taylor}_r(q) $ holds if and only if $ p = q $.

items.informal_name: Injectivity of Multivariate Polynomial Expansion Homomorphism for Positive Exponents
items.type: ∀ {σ : Type u_1} {R : Type u_3} [inst : CommSemiring R] {n : ℕ}, 0 < n → Function.Injective ⇑(MvPolynomial.expand n)
items.informal_description: For any commutative semiring $ R $ and type $ \sigma $, the algebra homomorphism that maps each variable $ X_i $ in the multivariate polynomial ring $ R[\sigma] $ to $ X_i^n $ is injective when $ n $ is a positive integer. This homomorphism preserves the algebra structure over $ R $ and raises each variable to the $ n $-th power.

items.informal_name: Injectivity of Expansion Homomorphism for Multivariate Polynomials
items.type:
∀ {σ : Type u_1} {R : Type u_3} [inst : CommSemiring R] {p : ℕ},
  0 < p → ∀ {f g : MvPolynomial σ R}, (MvPolynomial.expand p) f = (MvPolynomial.expand p) g ↔ f = g
items.informal_description: For any positive integer $ p $ and multivariate polynomials $ f, g $ over a commutative semiring $ R $ in variables $ \sigma $, if the expansion of $ f $ and $ g $ (each variable raised to the $ p $-th power) are equal, then $ f = g $. Symbolically, $ \text{expand}_p(f) = \text{expand}_p(g) $ implies $ f = g $.

items.informal_name: Injectivity of Polynomial Expansion: $ f(X) \mapsto f(X^n) $ for $ n > 0 $
items.type: ∀ {R : Type u} [inst : CommSemiring R] {n : ℕ}, 0 < n → Function.Injective ⇑(Polynomial.expand R n)
items.informal_description: For any commutative semiring $ R $ and any positive integer $ n $, the polynomial expansion map defined by substituting $ X $ with $ X^n $ is injective. This means that if two polynomials $ f(X) $ and $ g(X) $ satisfy $ f(X^n) = g(X^n) $, then $ f(X) = g(X) $.

items.informal_name: Shift automorphism on the polynomial ring
items.type: {R : Type u_3} → [inst : CommRing R] → R → Polynomial R ≃ₐ[R] Polynomial R
items.informal_description: For any commutative ring $R$ and any element $t \in R$, this defines an $R$-algebra automorphism of the polynomial ring $R[X]$. This automorphism maps a polynomial $p(X)$ to $p(X+t)$.

items.informal_name: Injectivity of Taylor Series Expansion at $ r $
items.type: ∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Ring R] (r : R), Function.Injective ⇑(Polynomial.taylor r)
items.informal_description: The Taylor series expansion map at $ r $, which sends a polynomial $ f(X) $ to $ f(X + r) $, is injective as a linear transformation on the polynomial ring $ R[X] $.

items.informal_name: Taylor Isomorphism for Polynomials over Commutative Rings
items.type: {R : Type u_1} → [inst : CommRing R] → R → Polynomial R ≃ₐ[R] Polynomial R
items.informal_description: For any element $ r $ in a commutative ring $ R $, the Taylor isomorphism is an $ R $-algebra isomorphism from the polynomial ring $ R[X] $ to itself that maps each polynomial $ f(X) $ to $ f(X + r) $. This equivalence preserves addition, multiplication, and scalar multiplication, with the inverse map given by substituting $ X - r $.

items.informal_name: Equality of Polynomial Algebra Equivalences via X + t Evaluation
items.type:

  Polynomial.algEquivAevalXAddC t = Polynomial.algEquivAevalXAddC t' ↔ t = t'
items.informal_description: For a commutative ring $R$ and elements $t, t' \in R$, the algebra equivalences defined by evaluating polynomials at $X + t$ and $X + t'$ are equal if and only if $t = t'$.

items.informal_name: Algebra Isomorphism Induced by Linear Polynomial $aX + b$
items.type: {R : Type u_3} → [inst : CommRing R] → (a : R) → R → [Invertible a] → Polynomial R ≃ₐ[R] Polynomial R
items.informal_description: For a commutative ring $R$ and elements $a,b \in R$ with $a$ invertible, the linear polynomial $aX + b$ induces an $R$-algebra automorphism of $R[X]$. This isomorphism is given by composition with $aX + b$, with inverse given by composition with $\frac{1}{a}(X - b)$, since their composition yields the identity polynomial $X$.

items.informal_name: Left Inverse Implies Injectivity on a Set
items.type: ∀ {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {s : Set α} {f : α → β} {f₁' : β → α}, Set.LeftInvOn f₁' f s → Set.InjOn f s
items.informal_description: If a function $ f : \alpha \to \beta $ has a left inverse on a subset $ s \subseteq \alpha $, then $ f $ is injective on $ s $. This means that for all $ x_1, x_2 \in s $, if $ f(x_1) = f(x_2) $, then $ x_1 = x_2 $.

items.type: ∀ {α : Sort u_1} {β : Sort u_2} [Nonempty α] {f : α → β}, Function.Injective f ↔ Function.HasLeftInverse f
items.informal_description: A function $ f $ is injective if and only if there exists a left inverse function $ g $ such that $ g(f(x)) = x $ for all $ x $ in the domain of $ f $.

items.informal_name: A function with a right inverse is injective
items.type: ∀ {α : Sort u_1} {β : Sort u_2} {f : α → β} {g : β → α}, Function.RightInverse f g → Function.Injective f
items.informal_description: If a function $ f : \alpha \to \beta $ has a right inverse $ g : \beta \to \alpha $ (i.e., $ f \circ g = \mathrm{id}_\beta $), then $ f $ is injective.

items.informal_name: Equivalence Constructions via Injective Function and Left Inverse are Equal
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_3} {β : Type u_4} (f : α → β) (f_inv : β → α) (hf : Function.LeftInverse f_inv f),
  Equiv.ofLeftInverse' f f_inv hf = Equiv.ofInjective f ⋯
items.informal_description: Given a function $ f : \alpha \to \beta $, a left inverse $ f_{\text{inv}} : \beta \to \alpha $, and a proof that $ f_{\text{inv}} $ is a left inverse of $ f $, the equivalence constructed by mapping $ a \in \alpha $ to $ f(a) $ using the left inverse coincides with the equivalence constructed directly from the injectivity of $ f $. This equality holds because the left inverse condition implies injectivity, making both constructions equivalent.
